$comment: Target ground truth for the IFSTTAR geophysical test site, as published in the
TU1208 Open Database of Radargrams paper.
PROVENANCE CLASS: transcribed_from_publication. Every value below was read by
hand from the open-access paper named in `sources`. The data archive on disk
(Zenodo 1211173) contains radargrams and instrument sidecars only, and no
target-geometry file of any kind -- its own index, List_Database_V1.ods, was
NOTHING HERE IS MEASURED, DERIVED OR INFERRED BY SUBTERRA, except where a
field carries `derived: true`, which states its derivation in words.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. No velocity. No time-zero. No depth computed from
a radargram. No detector label. The depths below are the experimental setup's
own account of what is buried where; they are the INPUT to a later validation
and must never become a training or scoring label.
READ THE DEPTH DATUM CAVEAT BEFORE USING ANY DEPTH. The published sections do
not draw the surface layers that were actually built on top of them.
verified_by_subterra_note: Subterra has excavated nothing and surveyed nothing here. Independent verification would mean a site visit or the authors' own survey records, neither of which this project has.

publication.citation: Dérobert, X.; Pajewski, L. TU1208 Open Database of Radargrams: The Dataset of the IFSTTAR Geophysical Test Site. Remote Sensing 2018, 10(4), 530.

site.name: IFSTTAR geophysical test site
site.location_described_as: Nantes research centre of IFSTTAR, France
site.description: a pit 30 m long and 5 m wide at its maximum depth (around 4 m), with sloping sides that extend the width of the site to about 20 m, divided into five regions filled with different homogeneous soils and hosting georeferenced targets

authors_terminology.depth: distances below the surface, printed on the transversal sections as negative numbers with 0.00 at the top
authors_terminology.transverse_offset: distances across the section, referred to by the authors as measured from 'the longitudinal axis of the test site'
authors_terminology.acquisition_line_offset: distance 'from the upstream border of the section', the authors' phrase

coordinate_frame.shared_with_radar_note: NO. The radargram files carry no site coordinate. Relating a trace index to a transverse offset needs the published profile length and scans-per-metre, and an along-line origin that no source states. Nothing here performs that association.
coordinate_frame.geographic_conversion: NOT SUPPORTED. The paper states the site surface 'was georeferenced on the longitudinal axis and on the sides, for every limit of the sections' but names no CRS, no datum and no coordinate. No offset here is converted to a geographic or projected coordinate.

target_geolocation_method.statement: During the realization of the test site, every embedded object was carefully geolocated, by using a theodolite. Therefore, each target is positioned from several points: 2 points on the upper side of the pipes at their beginnings and ends, 4 points at the upper angles of the polystyrene blocks, and from 3 to 20 points for the rock blocks and dolmens. The surface of the site was georeferenced on the longitudinal axis and on the sides, for every limit of the sections. For each half-section, an interpolation was performed from the 4 surface angles to obtain the height values above the various targets, and then calculate their respective depths.
target_geolocation_method.implication_for_pipe_depth_reference: The pipes were positioned from 2 points ON THE UPPER SIDE. Whether the printed layer depth is therefore to the pipe CROWN or to its CENTRE is not stated in words anywhere in the paper. See open question `pipe-depth-reference-surface`.

depth_datum_caveat.statement: It has to be mentioned that the top of this section was finalized with about 30 cm of limestone (material from the third region), due to lack of silty material; such layer is not represented on the scheme. Moreover, all transversal schemes of the geophysical test site presented in this Section do not show neither the 10-cm surface layer made in limestone nor the asphalt wearing course.
depth_datum_caveat.consequence: The 0.00 line printed on every transversal section is NOT necessarily the surface an antenna was dragged over. A 10-cm limestone surface layer and an asphalt wearing course are omitted from all five schemes, and the silt region additionally carries about 30 cm of limestone that is also not drawn. Any comparison of a published depth against a radar arrival must carry this, and it is one of the two reasons a time-zero cannot be read off this dataset for free.
depth_datum_caveat.quantified_note: 'about 30 cm' and '10-cm' are the paper's own words; the asphalt wearing course has no published thickness at all.

acquisition_lines.definition: Position: number identifying the acquisition line, which can be 1 (profile recorded 1.25 m from the upstream border of the section—left in Figure 2)/2 (3.75 m)/3 (6.25 m)/4 (8.75 m)
acquisition_lines.note: The paper says data were collected along eleven lines across the site; the nomenclature defines four line POSITIONS within a section. Only the four are numerically published, and only those are recorded here.

components.Optional1: 'h' added just before the position when a half-length profile is performed (e.g. h1)
components.Optional2: 'rev' when the profile is done in reverse
components.b: added before the extension for GPR 1 data recorded with the last-generation 200/400/900 MHz antennas, to distinguish them from data collected with older antennas at the same frequency

gpr_systems.GPR 1: GSSI (Geophysical Survey Systems, Inc; Nashua, NH, USA)

pipe_specification.$comment: One specification, stated for the silt region and referred back to by every other region.
pipe_specification.composition_and_order: three pipes per layer: an empty steel pipe, a PVC pipe full of water, and an empty PVC pipe (this is the laying order in all layers, starting from the longitudinal axis of the test site)
pipe_specification.diameter_note: The paper gives no diameter for the three-pipe layers in any region. The 10-cm PVC tubes mentioned in section 3.2 are drainage tubes in the pit's drainage layer, a different object, and are NOT used as a diameter here.
pipe_specification.spacing_statement: the distance between pipes pertaining to the same layer increases with depth

regions.figure_caption: Transversal section of the silt region, showing the embedded targets and their positions. All distances are expressed in meters.
regions.transverse_spacing_note: The consecutive segment lengths printed on the section's upper scale bar, left to right. Labels alternate above and below the bar for legibility. Their assignment to individual pipes is NOT recorded -- see open question `spacing-to-pipe-assignment`.

other_published_depths.note: One of the two depths printed for the staircase. Which of the six blocks it refers to is not printed.

modelled_permittivity.method: matching synthetic results of preliminary FDTD models with the measurements
modelled_permittivity.authors_caveat: Such estimations must be taken with care, as the surface limestone layer presents some slight thickness variations, and also because of the compaction performed on the silt above the polystyrene blocks during the test site implementation (which might have compressed the blocks a little). More advanced investigations will be carried out in the future, to obtain more accurate estimations of the various values.
modelled_permittivity.is_a_velocity_note: A permittivity is not a velocity and is not converted into one here. It is recorded so a later stage can compare a fitted velocity against an independent expectation, never so it can supply one.

regions.host_material: stratified: limestone / gneiss 0-20 / gneiss 14-20 / limestone / silt
regions.figure_caption: Transversal section of the multilayer region, showing the stratification of materials and the thicknesses of the layers.
regions.absence_attestation: There are five layers and no targets.
regions.absence_caveat: This is a control for EMBEDDED TARGETS, not a control for 'no reflector'. Five material interfaces are real reflectors and any detector will respond to them.
regions.layers_note: Thicknesses are printed inside each band of Figure 8. The figure prints 0.00 at the top and prints NO interface depth. Cumulative interface depths are therefore derivable but are not stored as published values -- see `benchmark.tu1208_truth.interface_depths`, which marks them derived.

boreholes.description: Two vertical holes allow carrying out borehole, crosshole and tomography investigations in this region of the test site.

regions.modelled_permittivity_note: None published. The paper states: 'The multilayer section remains a challenge for GPR specialists, to estimate the real thicknesses and permittivity values of the various layers.'

open_questions.statement: The theodolite survey positioned each pipe from '2 points on the upper side'. Whether the depth printed for a pipe layer is therefore the depth of the pipe CROWN or of its CENTRE is not stated. With no published pipe diameter, the two cannot even be related.
open_questions.magnitude: unknown; equal to one pipe radius, which is itself unpublished
open_questions.blocks: interpreting a fitted arrival time as crown depth or centre depth
open_questions.resolution_route: author contact, or the site's own survey records

open_questions.statement: The transversal sections omit a 10-cm limestone surface layer and the asphalt wearing course, and the silt section additionally omits about 30 cm of limestone. The printed 0.00 is therefore not established to be the surface the antenna travelled on.
open_questions.magnitude: at least 0.10 m site-wide and about 0.30 m more in the silt region, plus an unpublished asphalt thickness
open_questions.blocks: treating a published depth as a depth below the antenna without a stated correction
open_questions.resolution_route: author contact for the as-built surface levels

open_questions.statement: Each section prints a sequence of segment lengths on a scale bar above the pipe groups. Which segment separates which pair of pipes, and where the bar begins relative to the longitudinal axis, are not printed. The text's statement that 'the distance between pipes pertaining to the same layer increases with depth' is consistent with the sequence but does not by itself assign the numbers.
open_questions.blocks: any transverse localisation of an individual pipe
open_questions.resolution_route: a higher-resolution or vector original of the figures, or author contact

open_questions.statement: The limestone region is described as containing TWO series of pipe layers 'with the same properties as those embedded in the silt region'. The transversal section shows one series. Whether the second series lies at the same three depths is not published.
open_questions.blocks: counting limestone pipe targets above the nine shown in the section

open_questions.statement: Figure 13(b) prints four depths against the masonry symbol spanning 1.95 m, while the text describes two masonry walls, one of them with three steps and a total height of about 65 cm. Which printed depth belongs to which wall or step is unsettled.
open_questions.blocks: using any masonry depth as a target depth

open_questions.statement: The archive's own index, List_Database_V1.ods, was not packaged -- only its stale lock file. The file/region/line association therefore rests on the paper's Tables 3-7 and on the archive's directory layout, which agree.
open_questions.blocks: nothing at present; recorded because it removes one independent check
open_questions.resolution_route: obtain the index from the authors
